sections.content: You know the conditional for advice from A2 Unit 26. The new phrase here is *Si yo fuera tú*, + conditional, which presents the speaker's recommendation as a possible choice rather than an order. Learn *Si yo fuera tú* as a ready-made phrase: *fuera* is a form of the imperfect subjunctive, which comes later.

items.spanish: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con el profesor antes de cambiar de curso.
items.english: If I were you, I would speak to the teacher before changing courses.

items.spanish: Yo no aceptaría el trabajo sin leer el contrato con cuidado.
items.english: I would not accept the job without reading the contract carefully.

items.spanish: En tu lugar, buscaría una alternativa más segura.
items.english: In your position, I would look for a safer alternative.

items.spanish: Yo esperaría un poco más antes de decidir.
items.english: I would wait a little longer before deciding.

sections.content: Conditional advice is deliberately less direct than an imperative. It is especially natural when the speaker recognises that the final decision belongs to the other person.
